subject: Post-demo: output contract, auth & routing checklist
messages:
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@novumhealth.com>, Nick Lowe <nlowe@novumhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: output contract, auth & routing checklist

Thanks again for taking time today — quick consolidated recap and proposed next steps so your engineers have a concrete checklist to pick up. I focused this note on three areas you asked about: (1) auth & SDK bootstrapping, (2) routing/fallback behavior, and (3) output contract reliability (JSON enforcement + retry patterns).

High-level recap
- Goal: deterministic, parseable JSON from the generation step so your downstream pipeline and reranker can operate without ad-hoc parsing fixes.
- Constraints we discussed: low-latency for the user-facing path, occasional long-form reasoning for analytics batch jobs, and strict auditability of requests (request-id + retained prompts).

Auth & SDK setup (recommended)
- Use our SDK with server-side service account for ingestion endpoints. For end-user-scoped actions (e.g., personalized history retrieval) exchange short-lived session tokens via your backend (we recommend 1h TTL).
- Rotate keys via your KMS; SDK supports automatic refresh with client-side cached credentials. Add an x-redwood-request-id header for idempotency and tracing.
- Attachments: see auth-routing-checklist.md for example code snippets.

Routing and failover policy
- Primary route: hosted low-latency model (redwood-hosted/latest) for read/write endpoints.
- Canary: use header x-redwood-route: canary for experiments.
- Fallback policy: if primary latency spike (>350ms p95) or token quota reached, automatically route to a quantized variant (redwood-q4f) or to dedicated pool; fallback logic should prefer the variant with matching schema support.

Output contract / deterministic JSON approach (recommended pattern)
1) Strict contract: we propose an envelope with explicit versioning: {"contract_v": "1.0", "payload": {...}, "meta": {...}}. Contract schema attached as contract-schema-v1.json.
2) Deterministic decoding: set temperature=0 and sampling off where possible; for models that do not support exact determinism, set temperature<=0.1 and enforce top_p<=0.9.
3) Post-generation validation: run a JSON schema validator on the payload. If validation fails:
   a) first retry: internal repair pass — send the model a short instruction: "Output valid JSON matching schema X; here is the previous output. Please correct minimal syntax errors only." (1 quick attempt)
   b) second retry: re-generate with a smaller context (truncate non-essential system prompts) and route to the quantized but schema-aware variant.
   c) on repeated failure: return a structured error object to the caller explaining the failure category (parsing, missing required field, unexpected type).
4) Idempotency & observability: log both raw and validated payloads (redact PII), attach request-id and model-revision to logs for debugging.

Embeddings + reranker notes
- Use embedder to vectorize the candidate pool; compute embeddings server-side and cache top-K for frequently requested queries.
- Reranker should operate on top N (we suggest N=10) and expect the entries to conform to the same contract (payload fields used for scoring).
- If reranker needs additional context fields, include them in meta rather than payload to avoid schema drift.

Next steps (action items)
- PR: Redwood (Dev) to share concrete SDK snippets + token-exchange flow (auth-routing-checklist.md attached). (owner: dev_patel)
- PR: Redwood (Sales/AE) to schedule a brief infra sync to map network/firewall needs. (owner: marissa_cole)
- PR: Novum to confirm pilot scope (3 endpoints, expected qps, SLO targets). (owner: Samira)

Attachments: novum_demo_notes.pdf, auth-routing-checklist.md, contract-schema-v1.json

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m follow-up with your infra/ML engineers next week.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Fri, May 29, 2027 at 2:12 PM priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick consolidated recap and proposed next steps...

Thanks — added a few concrete engineering notes and an implementation sketch below so Novum's engineers can start implementing the pipeline immediately.

Implementation sketch (server-side)
- SDK boot: use the TokenExchange flow in our JS/Go SDK. Example: exchange your service account JWT for a short-lived session token (ttl=3600s). Store in in-memory cache with jittered expiry to avoid stampedes.
- Request envelope: include headers: x-redwood-request-id, x-novum-org, x-redwood-route. We use request-id to dedupe on retries.
- Retries/backoff: exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter. Parameters: initial=150ms, multiplier=2.0, max_attempts=3. Fail fast for auth errors (401/403).
- Validation loop: pseudocode:
   1) resp = client.generate(opts with temp=0.0, max_tokens=... )
   2) if is_valid_json(resp.text) and validate_schema(resp.json(), contract-schema-v1.json): return resp.json()
   3) else if attempts==1: call repair_prompt = \"Fix only the JSON so it matches schema X. Keep fields and types intact.\"; resp2 = client.generate(repair_prompt, options with stricter decoding)
   4) else: route to fallback model and set meta.error_hint = "fallback_regeneration"

- Function/tool-call support: if you use model function calling, treat tool outputs as separate, schema-validated artifacts; do not merge them into main payload without validation.

Performance tuning
- Batch reranker calls for offline scoring; keep online reranker to top-10. Cache embeddings with ttl 24h for high-frequency queries.
- Monitor p95/p99 for both generation and reranker; trigger autoscale at sustained p95>400ms for the generation cluster.

Deliverables from Redwood (by next Tue)
- Example Node/Go snippets for token exchange + schema validation.
- Minimal test harness that runs 50 synthetic requests and reports parse-failure rate.

Happy to pair with your infra engineer on network rules.

— Dev

Thanks — this is very helpful. I'll do the following today:
- Share our infra contact (Marta) and available windows for Tue/Wed (we prefer Tue 10:00-11:00 PT).
- Confirm the pilot scope: we want 3 read endpoints and 1 rerank endpoint, target 50 rps for the pilot.
- I'll also upload the initial security questionnaire to the Drive link you shared.

Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) For the repair prompt retry: how do you recommend we track attempted repairs vs original generation in logs? Can you add a flag in the SDK response (e.g., "repair_attempts": 0/1)?
2) For reranker caching: we need guidance on cache invalidation when source docs update. Is TTL sufficient or do you recommend hooks from our CMS?

We'll accept the pilot SOW but would like a short note in the SOW about model revision locks during the pilot (prevent automatic model rollout).

Samira
